source.title: Research Problem: The Completion Number of a Graph

accepted.question_text: For an undirected graph G = (V, E) with vertex set {1, 2, ..., n}, define a partial Hermitian matrix with graph G to be a matrix whose diagonal entries are specified real numbers and whose off-diagonal entries are specified exactly for the edges of G, with conjugate symmetry. Such a partial matrix is partial positive semidefinite when every specified principal submatrix is positive semidefinite. A Hermitian completion fills all unspecified entries, and i_-(M) is the number of negative eigenvalues of the completed Hermitian matrix M. The completion number of G is the smallest integer k such that every partial positive semidefinite matrix A with graph G has a Hermitian completion M with i_-(M) <= k. Given G, how can one determine this completion number, equivalently the minimum number of negative eigenvalues that can always be guaranteed in a completion, particularly for nonchordal graphs?
accepted.context_brief: Determining the completion number of a graph

evidence.quote: A partial matrix is a matrix in which some entries are specified and the others are left as free complex variables. A completion of a partial matrix is a conventional matrix obtained by the specification of all free variables. We call a matrix A = {aij} n i,j=1 partial Hermitian if aii is a specified real number for every i = 1, 2, · · · , n, aij is specified if and only if aji is specified, and ¯aji = aij .
A partial Hermitian matrix A is called partial positive (semidefinite) if all specified principal submatrices of A are positive.
The inertia of an n × n Hermitian matrix B is the triple (i+(B), i−(B), i0(B)), in which i+(B) (resp. i−(B)) is the number of positive (resp. negative) eigenvalues of B counting multiplicities
It appears as a potentially interesting question to ask what is the minimum number of negative eigenvalues one can always obtain in case of a given nonchordal graph.
Definition. Let G be an undirected graph. The completion number of G is the smallest number k such that every partial positive matrix A with graph G has a completion M with i−(M) ≤ k.
Question: Given a graph G, how can one find its completion number?

accepted.question_text: For each possible value k, can one give a graph-theoretic characterization of the undirected graphs G whose completion number is k, where the completion number of G is the smallest integer k such that every partial positive semidefinite Hermitian matrix A with graph G has a Hermitian completion M with at most k negative eigenvalues? In particular, chordal graphs are exactly the graphs with completion number 0, so the question asks for analogous graph-theoretic descriptions for other completion-number values.

evidence.quote: we ask for a graph theoretic characterization of those graphs with a given completion number.
Definition. Let G be an undirected graph. The completion number of G is the smallest number k such that every partial positive matrix A with graph G has a completion M with i−(M) ≤ k.

More specifically, it would be of interest to find graph theoretic characterizations of those graphs with given completion number. By the results in [3], the completion number of a graph G is 0 if and only if G is chordal.
